addmercrec: Defines one entry in a class's mercenary hiring pool: which monster can be offered, the percentage chance it shows up in an offer, how many units come together, and their cost in gold plus a variable gold-die bonus. Each entry can appear at most once within a given mercenary offer. The base game data also supplies a sixth value beyond the five the manual documents, and its purpose is not clear from the material.
addunitrec: Defines one entry in a class's regular unit recruitment list: which monster is recruitable, the percentage chance it is available, how many units can be recruited together, and their cost in gold (with a variable gold-die bonus) and iron.
animal: Classifies the monster, or the wearer of the item, as an animal: it can be harmed by weapons and spells restricted to affecting animals, and it leaves an animal carcass behind when it dies.
berserker: Gives the monster a chance to fly into a berserk rage once it is struck in combat, temporarily gaining Strength and Morale and allowing it to keep fighting even after taking heavy losses.
bramblegate: Marks the terrain's fort gate as a Bramble Gate, akin to how cloudgate sets a Cloud Gate. Not used by the base game data (0 attestations); the exact in-game effect is undocumented.
charmres: Grants immunity to charm effects, so the monster or item wearer cannot be magically charmed.
cloudgate: Sets the fort on this terrain to have a Cloud Gate as its entrance instead of an ordinary gate.
coldblood: Marks the monster as cold-blooded, giving it a Strength penalty while fighting on snow-covered ground.
deadforest1: Following the same 1/2 naming pattern used by the other terrain-affinity flags (e.g. desert1/2, jungle1/2), this presumably marks the monster as loving dead-forest terrain, so an independent or mindless commander with it would refuse to leave such ground. It has 0 attestations in the base game data, so this reading is inferred from the naming convention rather than confirmed by an in-game example.
deadforest2: By the same naming pattern as deadforest1 and the other paired terrain flags, this presumably marks the monster as merely liking dead-forest terrain, so an independent or mindless commander would stray no more than one square from it. It has 0 attestations in the base game data, so this reading is inferred rather than confirmed.
desert1: Marks the monster as loving desert terrain: an independent or mindless ("stupid") commander carrying this flag will refuse to move off desert squares.
desert2: Marks the monster as liking desert terrain: an independent or mindless commander carrying this flag will not stray more than one square from desert ground.
desert3: Marks the monster as disliking desert terrain, the opposite end of the same preference scale as the desert-loving and desert-liking flags; the base data gives no further detail on the exact mechanical consequence.
eastcoast: Restricts where the terrain can be placed on the map to coastal tiles only; despite the flag's name, it is not limited to the eastern coast and can appear along any coastline.
fast: Raises the monster's campaign-map action points to 4 and lets it take two movement actions per turn during tactical battles.
female: Marks the monster, or the item's wearer, as female — weapons restricted to affecting males (affectmale) cannot harm it.
gates1: Marks the monster as loving gateway terrain: an independent or mindless commander carrying this flag will refuse to move off gateway squares.
greedy: Stops the monster from ever voluntarily giving away its magic items. Not yet in the manual; the base game always writes it with an explicit value of 1.
human: Classifies the monster, or the wearer of the item, as human: it can be harmed by weapons and spells restricted to affecting humans, and it leaves a human corpse behind when it dies.
jungle1: Marks the monster as loving jungle terrain: an independent or mindless commander carrying this flag will refuse to move off jungle squares.
jungle2: Marks the monster as liking jungle terrain: an independent or mindless commander carrying this flag will not stray more than one square from jungle ground.
library1: Raises the location's library level by 1.
library2: Raises the location's library level by 2.
mines1: Marks the monster as loving mine terrain, so as an independent or stupid commander it will never move away from squares containing mines.
mountain1: Marks the monster as loving mountain terrain, so as an independent or stupid commander it will never move away from squares containing mountains. Never used in the base game data; behaviour inferred from the matching flags on other terrains (e.g. desert1, swamp1).
mountain2: Marks the monster as liking mountain terrain, so as an independent or stupid commander it will not wander more than one square from squares containing mountains.
nobootslots: Marks the monster as having no boot equipment slots, so it cannot be equipped with footwear items.
north1: Marks the monster as loving the far north, so as an independent or stupid commander it will never move away from squares in that region. Never used in the base game data; behaviour inferred from the matching pattern on other terrain-preference flags (e.g. south1/south2).
promoteunits: An event command that converts up to a given number of one monster type belonging to a player into a different monster type, effectively promoting those units. Never used in the base game data, so the exact selection and trigger conditions are undocumented.
ship: Marks the monster as a ship in sea battles; the value selects the size class — the base game passes 1 for normal-sized and 2 for large ships.
slimeshield: Gives the monster or item a slime shield: an opponent who strikes it in melee becomes slimed unless they pass a strength check.
south1: Marks the monster as loving the south, so as an independent or stupid commander it will never move away from squares in that region. Never used in the base game data; behaviour inferred from the matching south2 flag and the same pattern on other terrains.
south2: Marks the monster as liking the south, so as an independent or stupid commander it will not wander more than one square from squares in that region.
swamp1: Marks the monster as loving swamp terrain, so as an independent or stupid commander it will never move away from squares containing swamp.
swamp2: Marks the monster as liking swamp terrain, so as an independent or stupid commander it will not wander more than one square from squares containing swamp.
temple1: Marks the monster as loving temple terrain, so as an independent or stupid commander it will never move away from squares containing a temple. Never used in the base game data; behaviour inferred from the matching temple2 flag and the same pattern on other terrains.
temple2: Marks the monster as liking temple terrain, so as an independent or stupid commander it will not wander more than one square from squares containing a temple.
town1: Grants the location one town point, counted toward how many mercenary and merchant recruitment offers it can generate.
town2: Grants the location two town points, counted toward how many mercenary and merchant recruitment offers it can generate.
troll: Marks the monster as a troll, which changes how the Stygian Bath effect applies to it: instead of the usual partial resistance to piercing, slashing and blunt damage, it becomes fully invulnerable to non-magical attacks.
vengeance: Gives the monster a Blood Vengeance effect: anyone who damages it must pass a Magic Resistance check or take that damage themselves instead; a higher setting applies a penalty to that check, making the retaliation harder to avoid.
void2: Marks the monster as liking void terrain, so as an independent or stupid commander it will not wander more than one square from squares of that type.
